title: Crawler control decision input (v0.5, D57, MVP-29)
description: Input of the crawler-policy vectors: a bot catalogue, the crawler policy of one website (optionally with a preset applied), one request as the gate sees it and the gateway mode. The time is the vector context now (range snapshots older than 30 days are unknown_stale). The result is {bot, category, verification, rule, outcome, reason, status} (contract/crawlers.Decide). Every key of policy.bots must be a bot id of the catalogue, else the vector is invalid with code schema. Only user agents that name a catalogue entry can be blocked; likely_automated and likely_browser never are. Never sent anywhere.

preset.description: Applied to policy before the decision: the preset's categories replace the categories, the bot rules are dropped, impersonators stays (contract/crawlers.ApplyPreset).

user_agent.description: Empty when the request had none. Only the first 512 bytes are matched.

ip.description: Client address as the gate resolved it (documentation ranges in vectors).

mode.description: observe: the gateway runs the test profile and only records would_block (D89: there is no protection mode to set). autoblock: every other gateway.

allowlisted.description: The client address is on the allowlist (any level): never blocked, recorded as would_block.

category.description: Catalogue categories (bot-catalogue.schema.json). likely_automated and likely_browser are no crawlers and cannot be named.

preset.description: block_ai_training: block the category ai_training, allow every other category.

policy.description: What one website lets crawlers do. Absent keys allow: an empty policy changes nothing. A rule for a bot overrides the rule of its category. A block applies to every request whose user agent names that crawler, verified or not. impersonators block: a request that names a crawler whose operator publishes address ranges, from an address outside them (verification mismatch), is blocked whatever the other rules say.
